title: Anxiety & Overwhelm
description: When mind races with what-if scenarios, panic, and uncertainty about outcomes.
prescription: Focus entirely on the present action; release attachment to outcomes. The mind is turbulent, but controlled by practice and detachment.

verses.takeaway: You have right only to action, never to fruits. Be not anxious about results.
Pleasure and pain come and go like seasons. Learn to endure them with equanimity.
Doubtless the mind is restless, O Arjuna, but it is mastered by constant practice and detachment.
Abandon all worries and surrender in trust. I shall deliver you from all despair.

title: Burnout & Procrastination
description: When motivation is depleted, tasks feel meaningless, and lethargy takes over.
prescription: Action is superior to inaction. Perform your duty without ego-driven pressure, treating work as sacred dedication.

verses.takeaway: Perform your prescribed duty, for action is indeed better than inaction.
Constantly perform your duties without attachment; thus one attains the highest state.
He who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction, is truly wise among humans.

title: Anger & Frustration
description: When expectations are violated, leading to frustration, bitterness, and loss of composure.
prescription: Trace anger back to attachment. Control the senses before anger clouds intellect and ruins peace.

verses.takeaway: Brooding on objects creates attachment; attachment breeds desire; unfulfilled desire sparks anger.
From anger arises delusion, from delusion loss of memory, and thereby ruin of intellect.
One who can withstand the impulses of lust and anger before leaving the body is truly joyful.

title: Grief & Heartbreak
description: Coping with loss of loved ones, broken relationships, or shattered expectations.
prescription: The physical form is transient, but the soul is eternal, unkillable, and indestructible.

verses.takeaway: The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the departed.
The soul is never born, nor does it ever die; unborn, eternal, undying, it is not slain when the body dies.
Just as a person casts off worn-out garments and puts on new ones, the soul casts off worn-out bodies.

title: Decision Paralysis & Confusion
description: Stuck between hard choices, fearing making the wrong move or harming others.
prescription: Consult your higher self, establish a one-pointed intellect (Vyavasayatmika Buddhi), and act with integrity.

verses.takeaway: My heart is weighed down by confusion; tell me decisively what is best for me.
The resolute intellect is one-pointed; the intellect of the indecisive is many-branched.
Reflect on this wisdom thoroughly, and then act as you choose.

title: Finding Purpose (Swadharma)
description: Questioning your path, comparing yourself to others, or feeling lost in career and life.
prescription: Better is one’s own duty, though imperfect, than another’s duty well performed. Align action with your innate nature.

verses.takeaway: Better is one’s own duty, though devoid of merit, than the duty of another well performed.
By worshiping the Supreme through performance of one’s natural duty, a person achieves perfection.
One who performs duties dictated by natural inclination incurs no sin.
